entities.name: Rangjung Dorje, 3rd Karmapa Lama
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rangjung Dorje, the 3rd Karmapa Lama (1284–1339), was a pivotal figure in Tibetan Buddhism, leading the Karma Kagyu school and spreading Buddha-nature teachings across Tibet.

As head of the Karma Kagyu school, Rangjung Dorje played a crucial role in the development of Tibetan Buddhism, particularly during the 14th century. He strengthened ties between monasteries and laypeople, fostering a sense of community that would remain central to the tradition.

Rangjung Dorje's authority was further solidified through his diplomatic relationships with regional rulers, securing recognition for the Karma Kagyu school as one of the most prominent sects in Tibetan Buddhism. His leadership helped establish the school's global presence, attracting adherents from across Asia and beyond.

Despite facing challenges from rival factions and external threats to its authority, Rangjung Dorje's legacy endured, shaping the trajectory of Tibetan Buddhism for centuries to come.
